uncertainties: R1 is the baseline. Omission events report missing specifications, not forgetting or withdrawal of rules.
Honor, courage, gratitude, and stewardship do not unambiguously establish action motivated by moral identity; no moral_identity label is assigned.
R2 and R4 narrate equal final warmth; R5 narrates a greater-than-half return. These action differences are not rule transitions.
R4’s raven may propose a counterfactual to Lyra’s completed allocation or challenge allocation policy generally; no hypothetical/counterfactual feature is confidently assigned.
R4’s two burning lanterns are metaphorical scenery, not a confidently identifiable conjunctive policy trigger.
R5’s offered-trust condition is explicit, but whose trust must be offered is unspecified.
R6 contains divine teaching but no explicit communal law, pact, vow, or inherited custom; institution is not confidently assigned.
R7’s personal vow is an explicit commitment, not evidence that all senders adopt its scope.
R8’s repair practice is read as an endorsed communal custom from the law-following plural account, not merely approval of one act.
R8 and R10 answer greedy suggestions through actions rather than clear verbal exchanges; no challenge_dialogue label is assigned.
R9’s enduring-honor sending condition echoes R5’s faithful-keeper custom and later faithful-pattern prescriptions; it is not a new invention.
R9’s final-warmth measure does not necessarily reject giver-favoring returns or require exact equality.
Residual sparks, embers, lanterns, and seasons remain metaphorical; no literal numerical policy thresholds are inferred from them.
